- Measurement should be done at the same time every day for accurate tracking (Page 12)
- Blood pressure fluctuates within 1 hour after a meal, after using the toilet, after drinking alcohol and caffeine, when not quiet, after smoking, feeling stressed, after bathing, in extreme temperatures, or after exercise (Page 12)
- Long-time measurements can cause blood stasis; if this occurs, remove the watch, raise the arm high, and make a fist and open it about 15 times (Page 12)
- Home blood pressure measurements are often lower than hospital readings due to stress at hospitals or wrist position above the heart (Page 12)

- Measured values may be higher if the watch is not worn tightly, as pressure cannot reach blood vessels (Page 13)
- Incorrect postures like sitting cross-legged, on a low sofa, or placing the watch below the heart can result in higher measurements (Page 13)
- The product can be used as a reference in clinical practice but cannot serve as the basis for diagnosis (Page 13)
- Stop measurement immediately if uncomfortable due to excessive airbag inflation; do not keep the arm in the device when inflated (Page 13)
- Unfasten the strap if inflation pressure exceeds 300 mmHg (40 kPa) but does not deflate automatically (Page 13)

- Wait 10 minutes after going to the toilet and one hour after eating before measuring (Page 13)
- Avoid measuring in places with extreme temperatures or dramatic environmental changes (Page 13)
- Do not measure when standing, lying down, under pressure, or in a moving vehicle (Page 14)

- To record sleep on a phone, touch "Go to sleep" and place the phone within 50 cm of the pillow; press and hold "Hold to end" for 3 seconds to exit recording (Page 20)

- After enabling continuous skin temperature measurement, a measurement curve will be generated (Page 20)
